From: Elena Vasquez <elena@sentinel-tech.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-24 09:13 EST
Subject: Question: EU data locality + retention for hosted API

Hi Lauren,

We're in the final stages of our security review for Redwood as a hosted inference provider. A couple of quick, concrete questions the legal/security team asked — can you confirm these for the hosted API?

1) Can requests and derived artifacts be pinned to EU-only storage/processing? Which regions do you offer for EU residency?
2) What is the default retention (TTL) for request payloads, request/response logs, and embeddings? Can we change the TTL at the tenant level?
3) If we request deletion of a tenant's data, how quickly is the data removed from primary storage and from backups/snapshots?
4) Is data stored in backups ever used for training models?
5) Do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for hosted deployments, and will Redwood staff have access to raw plaintext if CMK is enabled?

We'd appreciate short, precise answers we can drop into our questionnaire. I've attached our questionnaire (spreadsheet) as well.

Thanks,
Elena
Security Operations
Sentinel Tech
Attachment: sentinel-ma-request-20270224.xlsx (XLSX, 38KB)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena@sentinel-tech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-25 11:02 EST
Subject: Re: Question: EU data locality + retention for hosted API

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers below are written to be copy/pasted into your questionnaire; I attached a short FAQ PDF with the same content plus links to our DPA. Monica is copied for any follow-ups on tenant configuration and Markus for technical validation.

1) EU-only processing and storage: Yes. For hosted API customers we offer region pinning to eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Customer requests routed to those regions are processed and stored in-region; metadata used for routing (minimal routing metadata) is replicated only as needed for operations and is retained per our retention policy (see below).

2) Default retention (TTL) and tenant-level controls: Default retention for customer request/response logs is 30 days. Embeddings and derived vectors are retained for 30 days by default. Customers on enterprise contracts can set a tenant-level TTL from 0 days (ephemeral) up to 365 days via a configuration flag; we can enforce shorter maxima as a contractual commitment.

3) Deletion timeline (primary storage and backups):
- Primary storage: When you submit a deletion request via the API or support portal we remove the tenant's objects from primary storage within 72 hours (we'll provide a purge job id).
- Backups/snapshots: Backups are retained as encrypted point-in-time snapshots for disaster recovery. Standard backup retention is 90 days; when a deletion event happens we mark snapshots containing the data for purge and they are removed within the next backup-cycle purge window (maximum 30 days from the deletion event). For expedited contractual commitments we can shorten backup purge windows to 7 days.

4) Training/Model usage: Redwood does NOT use customer-provided content passed through the hosted API to train or improve public models. We have an explicit policy preventing training on customer data; model training datasets are maintained separately.

5) Customer-managed keys (KMS): We support both Redwood-managed encryption keys and customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS in customer account or customer-supplied key managed through our control plane for private link setups). When customer-managed KMS is enabled, Redwood operators do not have access to plaintext; administrative access is controlled via key policies.

Extras:
- Audit logs: We capture API access logs and key administrative events for 365 days by default; these can be exported to your SIEM or pushed to an S3 bucket in your account.
- Data residency attestation: We can provide a region residency attestation signed by our security team as part of the DPA addendum.

Attachments: Redwood_Data_Residency_FAQ.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

If you want tighter contractual guarantees (shorter retention windows, faster backup purge), let me know and I can loop legal/eng to draft language for the SOW.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Thanks Lauren — that's helpful. Two quick clarifications before we close this out on our side:

• For backups: when you say "marked for purge and removed within the next backup-cycle purge window (maximum 30 days)", can you confirm the clock starts when Redwood confirms primary purge (i.e., when you provide the purge job id)? We need a clear deletion event timestamp.

• For KMS: can you confirm which parties can request key rotation or revocation when CMK is in use? Specifically, can Redwood support staff initiate a rotation request, or must the customer trigger it?

Appreciate the speedy responses.

—Elena
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena@sentinel-tech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-28 16:45 EST
Subject: Re: Question: EU data locality + retention for hosted API

Hi Elena — quick clarifications:

• Backups purge timeline: Correct — the deletion event timestamp is the time we confirm the primary purge and return the purge job id to your team. That timestamp is recorded and included in the deletion confirmation email. From that timestamp, backup purge windows are measured (standard maximum 30 days; expedited contractual purge windows are available).

• CMK rotation/revocation: With customer-managed KMS (key in your AWS account with a key policy granting Redwood access), key rotation can be initiated by the customer at any time. Redwood can request rotation operations as part of operational tasks but cannot complete rotation or revoke keys without an authorized customer action (per the KMS key policy). If you prefer, we can lock rotation privileges to customer principals only (we'll coordinate the exact key policy language with your security team).

Next steps: Monica can schedule a quick technical call to walk through tenant TTL configuration and show the deletion flow (we can demo issuing a purge job id in a staging tenant). Markus will follow up offline with a short engineering note on snapshot mechanics if you want more detail.

Thanks — happy to get any of this moved into contract language.

Best,
Lauren
